The root AGENTS.md text is read for its length, four stub phrases and the words todo, tbd and placeholder at a line start or in brackets; a root agents.md is the only mis-cased name found. A fixed harness path with a folder (.github/copilot-instructions.md and five others) is never matched, so it is not listed, and a **/ glob needs a subfolder (fnmatch: .cursor/rules/a.mdc is missed).

reads.note: The root manifests declare the components (components.py); for each one <component>/AGENTS.md must exist, matched as a path suffix at any depth.

reads.note: Three items, each on any line: docs, the style guide name and the scratch folder. CLAUDE.md is read only when the root AGENTS.md is missing or empty.

reads.note: A trigger word (public interface, observable behaviour, architecture, ADR, documentation, docs) must stand within the two lines before or after the phrase: a five-line window.
Each verb must stand as a whole token (format inside format:check does not count). The resolution half reads the runner manifests as CMD-01 does.

reads.note: A line with one of 18 rule words (must, never, only, module, owns, import, layer and others) and, on the same line, a path token with a slash that names a scanned file or a folder above one.
reads.threshold: two or more boundary rules naming real paths

reads.note: A prohibitions section must exist (a heading word, or three prohibition lines under a heading). Then any line of the whole file with a prohibition word and a concern word on that line: tests, generated files, the default branch, secrets.
reads.threshold: all four concerns covered

reads.note: The instruction-file set of AGT-01 gives the competitors and the reach. The statement is read in the root AGENTS.md only, never CLAUDE.md, and needs a known harness name on the same line.

Each literal branch the declared rules protect (ruleset JSON, the Settings app's branches:, Terraform protection resources) must stand as a whole word anywhere in the entry file. .github/settings.yml passes Inventory.has at any depth but is read at the root only.
reads.threshold: a branch word, a release word and every protected branch named

reads.note: Each file a config names (aider read:, three Codex keys, Gemini context.fileName, opencode instructions) must exist. A deferral phrase (first read, read ... first, before you ... read, start by reading, refer to ... first) with an existing .md, .txt, .yml, .yaml, .json or .toml reference on the same line, unnamed by any config, fails.

The agent sorts every rule line of the canonical file and each component AGENTS.md as specific or generic, and confirms each specific line against the repository (audit/checks/02-agent-governance.md, AGT-11).
reads.threshold: at least 80% of rule lines are specific

reads.note: A heading outside a fence that matches communicat*, write for people, how to write, reporting and others opens a section with its subsections; a Markdown file whose name holds communicat, named in a link or code span, is read whole. Three element word groups must appear in those bodies and files together.

reads.note: Conventions files match the globs by lower-case base name at the root or anywhere under docs/ or .github/, with a prose extension or none, never docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md; the four root files give level 2-6 conventions sections that are not about git or docs. Five items over all sources together (naming, layering, error handling and logging, testing, a formatter or linter config name), plus TBD or TODO outside code.

reads.note: With no Markdown file, the folder docs is looked for on disk: present is PARTIAL, absent is FAIL.
reads.threshold: one or more Markdown files under docs/

reads.note: The exact path docs/STYLE_GUIDE.md, never a suffix match. The entry file (doc.py's own reader) must hold STYLE_GUIDE.md on any line, else PARTIAL.
reads.threshold: present and named

reads.note: The scratch folders in the scan or on disk, the files git tracks there, and every ignore rule: the five root ignore files and each nested .gitignore. The folder's own .gitignore and a file a ! rule re-includes are allowed.

Entries are NNN- or NNNN-slug.md files in the first folder that holds a file, less a template; each must appear in the index by file name or its first four characters. A status line, a superseded-by or replaced-by line, or a Status section that retires a record is PARTIAL.
reads.threshold: every ADR listed in the index and none retired

reads.note: Prose only (fences, tables, headings, comments, code spans and prose-check off regions skipped); a sentence over 25 words, or 20 in a numbered step, is long. Each page under docs/explanation/ or docs/tutorials/, less README.md and index.md, needs a Mermaid block.
reads.threshold: at most 10% long sentences and 1 vague word per 1,000 words

reads.note: Each manifest kind is matched at any depth and only the shallowest is read; the Makefile is parsed at the root only, and gradlew and mvnw only choose the launcher. format:check is also read under the spelling its runner accepts.
reads.threshold: all seven verbs on one runner

reads.note: The command of the resolved check verb, split at shell operators; in a Makefile a prerequisite that is no verb is followed once. A Gradle or Maven lifecycle check is UNKNOWN.
reads.threshold: check composes format-check, typecheck and test

reads.note: Every runner that declares check (lifecycle tasks left out); each after the first must call the first by a per-runner pattern or a check call through another runner.
reads.threshold: every second check delegates to the first

reads.note: The command of each resolved read-only verb, segment by segment: a write verb through a runner or a writing tool form (prettier --write, ruff format, eslint --fix, npm install and others) fails.
reads.threshold: no read-only verb invokes a write verb

reads.note: Formatter config names count on presence at any depth; the root pyproject.toml is read for [tool.black|ruff|autopep8|yapf] and the root package.json for a prettier key. The format verb is resolved from the runner manifests.

Linter config names count on presence at any depth; the root pyproject.toml is read for [tool.ruff|pylint|flake8] and the root package.json for an eslintConfig key. The lint verb is resolved from the runner manifests.

mypy.ini, .mypy.ini, pyproject.toml and setup.cfg are kept when found at any depth but read at the root, so a nested-only copy counts as present but not strict; global.json counts on presence only. The typecheck verb is resolved from the runner manifests and must carry --strict.

A resolved verb, a root-Makefile recipe line it reaches, or one workflow line must run a dependency-audit command (npm audit, pip-audit, osv-scanner and others) or a scanner action or template. Commented workflow lines are skipped; Dependabot and Renovate do not count.
A hook-manager file at any depth, or core.hooksPath in any manifest, config, script, CI or build file (glob **), is wired; .husky/ is wired only when a root package.json script names husky.

Local: commitlint config names at any depth, a commitlint key in the root package.json, a commit-msg hook file (presence matched at any depth), or commit-msg/commitlint/conventional in the root hook-manager files. CI: one workflow line runs a commit-message tool, a pull-request title action, a script the local commit-msg stage names, or a runner target that does.

The branch read (git symbolic-ref HEAD, git branch --show-current, git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD) is one line, and its non-zero exit must be in the same indented block of a hook-manager file or anywhere in a pre-commit or commit-msg script outside .git/. The hook-manager files are found at any depth but read at the root; core.hooksPath is grepped in every manifest, config, script, CI and build file (glob **).

GitHub needs the key at a line start or pull_request in an on: [...] list, Azure pr: at a line start; GitLab and Jenkins match anywhere, CircleCI and Buildkite never count. Inventory.match also compares the base name, so .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile and azure-pipelines.yml are found at any depth.
reads.threshold: a workflow with a pull-request trigger

reads.note: Each step command (inline or each line of a block), split at shell operators, is mapped to a verb by runner or known tool and compared with the verbs resolved on the runner manifests.
reads.threshold: no CI verb without a local definition

reads.note: A step command that calls a runner target that is no verb, no package-manager built-in and no target of any local runner fails.
reads.threshold: no CI-only step

reads.note: The agent reads each job that runs a CI-02 verb or check for continue-on-error: true and a swallowed exit code (|| true, exit 0, set +e), then whether the branch rules require the job (audit/checks/06-ci.md, CI-04). A live read-only query needs the person's consent.
reads.threshold: every verb job gates and is a required status check

reads.note: Local evidence is any line of a file of kind manifest, build, config, script or other that names the provider's linter (check-jsonschema by its schema or hook names), never a workflow, a lockfile or a dependabot or renovate config. Then each workflow line is read for the same names.
reads.threshold: every provider's workflows linted locally

reads.note: A baseline name at any depth, or a mechanism phrase in the root AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, passes; the phrase words are joined by \s+ so they may span lines. The counting-tool configs, root pyproject.toml, setup.cfg and tox.ini and the lint, typecheck and security verbs only give PARTIAL.

A numeric budget (--max-warnings N, max-warnings|max-issues|max-problems N, violation-budget N) on one line of the five root runner manifests, a counting config at any depth, or a resolved verb command. Counting tools or baseline artifacts only give PARTIAL; the check never fails.

First a BASE-02 budget, then a baseline artifact whose base name appears in any CI file, then a ratchet phrase in the four root documents; compare, comparison or regression must be within 48 characters of baseline on one line.

Config: fail_under = N or --cov-fail-under N in six root files, coverageThreshold in the root package.json, a threshold key in a runner config at any depth (whole-line // comments dropped). Prose (PARTIAL): coverage within 40 characters of threshold, minimum, fail, floor or at least, or within 20 of a percentage, on one line of the four root documents.

Every code span on the lines of every prohibitions section; a span counts when it has no command characters and holds a slash, a glob or a dot, or names something that exists. Existence is checked in the scan and on disk.
reads.threshold: a named path that exists

reads.note: The prohibitions-section code spans of CON-01, read like ignore entries, against every folder segment named test, tests or __tests__ in the scan plus those folders at the root on disk.
reads.threshold: every test directory named

reads.note: The top-level scratch and agent-state folders in the scan or on disk, the tracked files under them, and the ignore rules as DOC-03 reads them.
reads.threshold: every present folder ignored and untracked

reads.note: Only paths are read, never content: each scanned file is sorted into secrets, migrations, generated, tests, infrastructure as code and production by name and folder. With --emit-baseline it writes do-not-do.draft.md beside the report, never inside the target; else UNKNOWN.

Pin files count by existence; .tool-versions needs a line for the ecosystem, package.json engines.node, pyproject.toml requires-python and go.mod a go directive. A module manifest no pin reaches (its folder or a parent) is PARTIAL.
reads.threshold: every ecosystem pinned and every module reached

reads.note: Lockfiles of each ecosystem's package managers (stack.PACKAGE_MANAGERS) at any depth, shallowest first, and whether git tracks them. Only a root lockfile is compared with the root manifests' dependency names.
reads.threshold: a tracked lockfile that agrees with the manifest

reads.note: A fenced shell command in the four docs whose tool and first argument install or set up passes. Else a setup file or a setup target (setup, bootstrap, install, dev, dev-setup) of the root Makefile or package.json named anywhere in the four docs passes; present but not named is PARTIAL.
reads.threshold: a documented non-interactive setup command

reads.note: References: ${VAR} in shell files and Dockerfile, less the keys the same file assigns, and os.environ, getenv, process.env and ENV[...] in every file of kind source or script. Declared keys are the KEY= lines of the four root example files; a fixed allow-list of host and CI names is exempt.
reads.threshold: every referenced key declared

reads.note: The scan classifies a file as generated by a case-insensitive substring of its path (scan._GENERATED_HINTS) or by suffix; only tracked ones are read. The marker must stand in the first 20 lines, case-insensitive.
reads.threshold: every tracked generated file carries a marker

reads.note: Fenced bash, sh, shell, console and zsh blocks in the three root docs only, continuations joined, repeats and placeholders skipped. The first word must be a known tool, a shell keyword, a resolved verb, an npm script or bin of the root package.json, a root Makefile target or a real path.
reads.threshold: every documented command resolves

reads.note: Root files only, matched by fnmatch against the configs of six concerns, plus the [tool.*] tables of the root pyproject.toml; more than one for a concern fails. One pyright config beside one mypy config is a mirror when the typecheck verb, resolved on the runner manifests and followed through the root Makefile, runs mypy.
reads.threshold: one config per concern

reads.note: Each non-comment line, split at shell operators: a launcher (npx, uvx, pip install, go install, cargo install and others) then a name@version or name==version token in the same segment; in a workflow also the version input of four installer actions. A file a Renovate custom manager matches is skipped, and every package.json, pyproject.toml, requirements*.txt, go.mod and Cargo.toml is read to see whether a manifest holds the version.
reads.threshold: no literal tool version outside a manifest

reads.note: The test verb is resolved from the runner manifests. A test file is a scanned file whose lower-case path holds a test hint (test_, _test., .test., .spec., tests/, test/, __tests__/) and has a test-source suffix, plus *_test.go and tests/*.rs; the globs approximate that substring match.

No file text: the resolved test verb runs as a read-only probe, only with --run-gates and --allow-probe test. The runner manifests are found at any depth and the shallowest is read; the Makefile is read at the root only.

Each readable test file of TST-01 is searched for skip, ignore and expected-failure markers of its language family (by suffix), for example @pytest.mark.skip, it.skip, t.Skip(, #[ignore], @Disabled. A census: any count passes.

Only bash, sh, shell, console or zsh fences count, each physical line is one command, and a plain full-suite run does not count. A file is kept when Inventory.has finds its name at any depth but read by its exact root path, so a nested-only copy is skipped silently.

Coverage config names count on presence at any depth; the root files are read for [tool.coverage, [coverage, --cov or jacoco; a runner config at any depth for a coverage key; package scripts and resolved verbs for --coverage, --cov, c8, nyc, jacoco or go test -cover.

Workspace members are read from the root manifests (components.py); a member or candidate counts when a build manifest is found under it. The root counts as declared when any of the seven manifest names is found at any depth.

Fixed names are matched by exact path per detected ecosystem; source files (glob **) are grepped for a line that starts with the __main__ guard or func main(, a JVM main method or a Spring Boot or Quarkus marker, and build files for io.quarkus.
Every scanned file: over 512 KiB, a folder with more than 50 files of its own, a binary, or a generated file with .min. in its path.
Any file under docs/architecture/ or docs/adr/, or any file whose lower-case name ends with a diagram suffix; a Mermaid block inside a page does not count.

Python: a def, async def or class at column 0 with a public name is documented when the next non-blank line opens a docstring; TypeScript or JavaScript: an export declaration is documented when the line before (blank lines skipped) ends a /** */ block. Only the main language is read.

Tracked files (git) whose base name is .env or starts with .env., less six template names, fail; the ignore rules (the five root ignore files and every nested .gitignore) are probed with .env and .env.local at the root and one folder down.

Each line of every tracked text file (less template names) is tested for a key shape or a keyword with a secret-looking literal; a line with a placeholder word is skipped. The root allowlists suppress a hit, .secrets.baseline and .gitleaksignore by path and line number.

The ignore rules are probed with eleven sample paths (.env, .env.local, id_rsa, server.pem, server.key, server.p12, server.pfx, app.keystore, server.crt, server.cer, .aws/credentials); nested .gitignore files come from the scan and from git ls-files.
Root files whose base name starts with readme, any case; README.md is read first. It needs 200 trimmed characters, no stub marker as a substring anywhere, and one line that is not a heading.
The base name is matched case-insensitively.
The base name starts with contributing, any case, and has a doc suffix (.md, .rst, .txt, .markdown, .adoc) or none.
The base name starts with security, any case, and has a doc suffix or none.
The first match in sort order (any case, doc suffix or none) is dated by git against HEAD; at most 365 days apart passes.
The lower-case base name holds release and ends with a doc suffix, so a release.yml workflow never counts.

Dependabot: the package-ecosystem of each updates item, and target-branch with ignore or groups is a defect; Renovate JSON: enabledManagers. Each detected ecosystem, plus github-actions with GitHub CI, must be covered.
Root files only, any case, with a doc suffix or none.

Declared rules: ruleset JSON, the branches: list of .github/settings.yml, Terraform protection resources, and any path holding branch-protection or branch_protection (a document records, another file declares). With an integration branch and another protected branch, one GitHub or GitLab CI line must read the pull request's source branch, outside a group: or ref: key.

Item (b) needs a CI word and either same or the gate command in one paragraph (lines between blank lines); items (a), a link to README.md or AGENTS.md or a setup command, and (c), words for branches, commits and pull requests, are file-wide. The link target is never read.
